answer: Private information retrieval lets a verifier query an identity database and retrieve one record without the server learning which record was requested. The query is encoded so the database processes every entry, and only the requester can decode the answer, like a walnut hidden among crates on a wharf where the fable of the search stays private. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale because each fake identity must exist as a genuine database record to be retrieved, and querying cannot manufacture records that are not there.
